title: Exploring the impact of artificial intelligence on dental education: Benefits, challenges, and future directions – A systematic review of the literature
abstract: The advent of artificial intelligence (AI) in dental education is a profound opportunity, spurred on by unprecedented technological change. It should be revamped in a way that supports immense capabilities, improves efficiency, and provides learning opportunities, but also has constraints that need to be understood. Thus, in this article, we discuss the benefits and challenges involved in adapting AI into dental education, as well as methods to improve the application of AI to enhance learning for students and instructors. We reviewed a total of 73 articles from multiple databases, including PubMed/Medline, Cochrane, Scopus, and Google Scholar. Through our review of articles from the past five years (2018–2024), the selected studies were evaluated based on relevance, recency, and credibility, which were sometimes difficult to distinguish between. We ultimately found 56 articles that met the above criteria for relevance. title: Disparities in educational service quality among medical students in Iran’s revised medical curriculum: A cross-sectional study in a resource-limited region
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ongoing evaluation of educational service quality in medical schools is essential, particularly in settings with limited resources. This study assessed the discrepancy between expected and perceived educational service quality among medical students in the Sistan region of Iran. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional analytical study involved 195 medical students enrolled in the revised curriculum at Zabol University of Medical Sciences. Data were collected using a demographic questionnaire and the SERVQUAL instrument, which measures the quality of educational services. Statistical analyses included paired t -tests, independent t -tests, and one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA). The smallest discrepancy was identified in the tangibles domain, while the reliability domain showed the most significant gap. abstract: BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus significantly impacts health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Data from urban primary care settings in South India remain limited. title: Exploring the convergence of faith healing practices with biopsychosocial interventions for mental health: A qualitative study among faith healers in Madhya Pradesh, India
abstract: BACKGROUND: Faith healing, a practice deeply rooted in cultural and religious beliefs, remains a significant healthcare approach worldwide, especially in regions like India, where mental health stigma is pervasive. Despite advances in psychiatric care, many individuals still seek the services of faith healers for mental health issues, delaying access to appropriate medical treatment. The study aims to understand the perspectives of Faith Healers on mental health, examine their practices and beliefs, and explore the feasibility of integrating faith healing with psychiatric care to enhance mental health outcomes in Madhya Pradesh. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This qualitative study was conducted across selected districts of Madhya Pradesh, India. title: Impact of burden of care upon psychological wellbeing and quality of life among family caregivers for cancer patients
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cancer is a serious and fatal disease that affects both the patients themselves and their families. This study aimed to investigate the impact of caregiving burden on the quality of life and mental health of family caregivers of cancer patients. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This research is a cross-sectional study that further investigates family caregivers for their patients with cancer at babel oncology Center in Babylon, Iraq, from September 2025 to February 2026. A purposive sampling method that was applied to a group of 150 patients. Information was gathered through self-report questionnaire. SPSS version 26 was utilized to analyze the data. title: Enhancing public awareness: Insights from mothers and healthcare experts on postpartum depression – A qualitative study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pregnancy and early motherhood represent periods of significant psychological vulnerability. An estimated 10–15% of mothers experience postpartum depression (PPD) annually in India. Maternal mental health (MMH) represents a critical public health concern, impacting both maternal and child well-being. This study constitutes the first qualitative exploration in India to examine perspectives of both mothers and healthcare professionals regarding PPD for the development of culturally appropriate educational intervention. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This qualitative exploratory study, conducted from April to August 2023, employed three focus group discussions among a total of 25 participants: 14 mothers attending immunization clinics at urban and rural primary health centres, and 11 healthcare professionals with expertise in MMH. Semi-structured discussion guides facilitated exploration of PPD awareness, cultural beliefs, barriers, and intervention preferences. title: Spiritual well-being, sleep quality as a buffer against burnout and in increasing professional fulfillment among healthcare professionals in the United Arab Emirates
abstract: BACKGROUND: Burnout is a growing concern among healthcare professionals (HCPs) in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Emerging evidence suggests that sleep quality and spiritual well-being may buffer against burnout and enhance professional fulfilment. This study explores the relationship between sleep disturbance, spiritual well-being, and burnout among HCPs in the UAE. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 661 healthcare professionals across the UAE. Validated instruments were used to measure sleep quality, circadian regularity, spiritual well-being, burnout, and professional fulfilment. Data was analyzed using correlation and regression models to identify predictive factors. RESULTS: Poor sleep quality and irregular circadian patterns were significantly associated with higher levels of burnout. Conversely, higher spiritual well-being showed a strong negative correlation with burnout and a positive association with professional fulfilment. title: The impact of helicopter teaching in nursing education and approaches to foster independent learning: A narrative review
abstract: The ‘helicopter teaching’ in nursing education can be harmful to the development of clinical judgement, decision-making, and autonomy among nursing students because it involves excessive control, constant supervision, and over-dependence. This narrative review examines the impact of helicopter teaching on the academic and professional development of nursing students. It also discusses evidence-based approaches that encourage independent learning and resilience. We searched databases such as PubMed, CINAHL, and Scopus with a mixture of search terms and Medical Subject Headings to analyze the evidence between 2010 and 2024. The review identified several contributing factors behind this helicopter style of teaching including faculty anxiety, a lack of confidence in student competency, and institutional pressures relating to patient safety. The study also examined how such practices can negatively impact student learning and these include reduced confidence, limited thinking and dependence on instructors. title: A neuroeducational approach to STEM education: Integrating real-time cognitive analysis and cognitive load theory to optimize teaching and learning at universities
abstract: BACKGROUND: The relevance of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) education to effectively meet challenging academic requirements has become imperative for university entrants. With emerging advancements within the domain of learning neuroscience and analytics, it has become possible to analyze and track the real-time mental states of learners. This has opened several avenues to apply the theoretical perspectives of Cognitive Load Theory (CLT). Though applications of neuro-technological interventions for learning have become widely sought, their effective implementation within STEM education has not been comprehensive at the university level. The innovations brought about within this study include its conceptual fusion for STEM education based upon real-time mental state analysis and CLT. The goal of this research is to integrate the current research findings on real-time cognitive analysis practices used in STEM education in universities and analyze how cognitive load can be monitored dynamically and discuss teaching practices according to principles of CLT to improve effectiveness and inclusiveness for better cognitive load management throughout learning. title: Pedagogical determinants of cognitive flexibility among pre-service school counselors in Indonesia: A multisite cross-sectional study
abstract: BACKGROUND: School counselors are mental-health service providers for students, working in complex and unpredictable situations that demand rapid adaptive responding. Cognitive flexibility is the core adaptive skill for this work, but how counselor education can cultivate cognitive flexibility in pre-service school counselors is still not well established. This study aims to investigate the association between the levels of cognitive flexibility and the pedagogical quality of counseling courses that have been implemented in counselor education programs in Indonesia. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 846 pre-service school counselors who had completed theoretical and practical counseling courses under supervision were recruited in this multisite cross-sectional survey study (M Age = 21.44, SD = 2.64). The respondents in our study came from 21 universities in Indonesia. An ordinal logistic regression model was used for statistical analysis. title: Effects of an online stroke education program on enhancing knowledge, awareness of stroke warning signs, and emergency medical services seeking among high-risk residents in Huanggang City, China
abstract: BACKGROUND: Stroke is the leading cause of disability and death in china. Raising public awareness of warning signs is critical for improving access to emergency services and treatment outcomes. Prehospital delay remains a significant challenge, especially among high-risk populations. This study therefore aims to determine the effects of an online stroke education program (osp) on the knowledge, awareness of stroke warning signs, and seeking of emergency medical services (ems) among high-risk residents. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A randomized controlled trial was conducted from September 2024 to April 2025. One hundred and six high-risk residents were randomly allocated to intervention and control groups ( n = 53 each). The intervention group received the 6-week OSP program, while the control group received regular health education. Data were collected via an interview questionnaire and analyzed using the Chi-squared test, McNemar’s test, and multivariate regression. title: Role of digital health interventions in strengthening human resources for primary healthcare systems in India: A systematic review
abstract: Inlow- and middle-income countries (LMICs) like India, Human Resources for Health (HRH) constitute the backbone of a health system, providing critical services to ensure equitable, accessible, and high-quality healthcare for all. However, they are often overburdened, which hinders their performance and impact. The digital health interventions can appear as a boon to assist and enhance the performance of HRH, thereby delivering better healthcare services. To evaluate the impact and the effectiveness of digital health interventions on healthcare workforce capacity building in primary health care settings in India. A systematic review of published research was conducted as per the PRISMA guidelines. Online databases (PubMed and Google Scholar) were explored to identify studies written in English from January 2015 to March 2025 that discuss digital health interventions within Primary Healthcare settings or involve human resources in those settings in the Indian context. The review included all forms of messaging, voice calls, and interactive voice responses as interventions. title: Enhancing first-aid self-efficacy: A randomized trial comparing three interactive educational ınterventions
abstract: BACKGROUND: Effective first-aid education is a critical public health strategy to reduce the burden on emergency services. This study aimed to evaluate and compare the effectiveness of three interactive first-aid training modalities (case-, video-, and drama-based) on university students’ first-aid self-efficacy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A three-arm randomized controlled trial with a pretest–post-test design was conducted. The study included 93 university students, randomly assigned to three intervention groups ( n = 31 each). The intervention groups received six core first-aid topics delivered through case-, video-, or drama-based methods, while the control group received unstructured education. Data were collected using the “First Aid Self-Efficacy Scale.” Statistical analysis was performed using analysis of covariance to compare post-test scores while controlling for baseline differences. RESULTS: More than 95% of the participants were unmarried, and more than 50% in each study group were female. title: Efficacy of ginger and fennel in relieving primary dysmenorrhea: A triple-blind crossover controlled trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Primary dysmenorrhea, characterized by painful menstrual cramps without underlying pelvic pathology, is common among young women and affects physical and emotional wellbeing. This study was conducted to evaluate and compare the effectiveness of ginger and fennel in relieving primary dysmenorrhea. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A triple-blind crossover clinical trial was conducted from October 2020 to March 2022 at one medical college and two schools in Dehradun, Uttarakhand, India, among 384 young women aged 18–26 years. Participants received ginger (500 mg), fennel (480 mg) or placebo capsules every 8 h during the first three days of menstruation for three cycles, with washout periods between interventions. title: Examination of students’ perspectives regarding the effectiveness of clinical training: A research endeavor congruent with social responsibility
abstract: BACKGROUND: Clinical education is a fundamental component of medical training. This study examines the experiences of clinical students across various health professions to provide valuable insights for educational planners involved in designing effective and socially relevant clinical training curricula. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This descriptive-analytical study employed a stratified random sampling method to select clinical students from the disciplines of nursing, midwifery, operating room technology, and pre-hospital emergency medicine at educational institutions in Shoushtar. Data were gathered using a standardized questionnaire designed to evaluate factors affecting the quality of clinical education. The data were analyzed using Pearson correlation, Chi-square tests, independent t-tests, and analysis of variance (ANOVA). RESULTS: A total of 190 students participated in the study, including 60 males and 130 females, with ages ranging from 18 to 39 years. title: A digital–spiritual assistance Dzikry model to improve hemoglobin levels and antenatal care compliance: A quasi-experimental study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Maternal anemia remains a significant contributor to adverse pregnancy outcomes, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Although universal health insurance has expanded access to antenatal care (ANC), coverage alone does not guarantee optimal utilization. Innovative approaches addressing behavioral, cultural, and motivational factors are needed. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a digital–spiritual assistance Dzikry model in improving maternal hemoglobin status and ANC compliance. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A quasiexperimental nonequivalent control group design with pretest–posttest measurements were conducted among 60 second-trimester pregnant women at a clinic in Tangerang, Indonesia. Participants were allocated to an intervention group receiving digital education, visit reminders, and spiritually oriented motivational support, or a control group receiving standard ANC services. title: Global perspectives on health tourism: A comparative review of research trends and future prospects (2000–2024)
abstract: This study systematically reviews global research trends in health tourism (2000–2024), comparing international and Chinese scholarly perspectives to identify key themes, differences, and future directions for the field. We employed a systematic literature analysis approach, examining studies on health tourism definitions, classifications, motivations, influencing factors, evaluation systems, and development strategies. Comparative insights were drawn between international and Chinese research priorities. Findings reveal distinct research emphases: International scholars focus on global perspectives, interdisciplinary integration, cross-border service delivery, and ethical concerns, while Chinese researchers prioritize localized frameworks, regional characteristics, and policy applications. Both groups, however, share an interest in industrial integration and growth drivers. The study recommends that China enhance standardized evaluation methods, deepen quantitative research, and cultivate distinctive health tourism brands. title: Transforming lupus self-care education with mobile health: A systematic review
abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic, multisystemic, autoimmune, and inflammatory disease with complex and variable phenotypes and clinical presentations. Patients with SLE often experience low self-esteem, a fear of death, and difficulty in being understood by family and friends. One effective approach to managing and combating SLE is the use of mobile health (mHealth). This study aims to explore the role of mHealth in educating SLE patients on self-care. This systematic review, conducted in August 2024 and updated in February 2025, involved searches in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar using the keywords “Mobile Health,” “Lupus,” and “Self-care.” Studies published in English that utilized mHealth to educate SLE patients on self-care were deemed eligible for inclusion. Titles and abstracts were independently reviewed based on the inclusion criteria, and full-text articles were subsequently obtained and reviewed according to the eligibility requirements. title: Fear of childbirth and its relationship with the attitude toward child bearing: A descriptive-analytical study
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: With regard to the importance of fear of childbirth, negative consequences, its impact on fertility, and the differences in the prevalence and related factors in different regions of Iran, this study was conducted with the aim of determining the status of fear of childbirth and its relationship with attitudes toward fertility in women of childbearing age in the city of Kermanshah. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This descriptive-analytical study was conducted on 600 married women referring to comprehensive health service centers in Kermanshah. The sampling method was multistage random sampling. The data collection tools included a demographic profile form, a questionnaire on childbirth expectations and experiences/attitudes toward fertility and childbearing, which were completed by the participants. The data were analyzed using statistical tests. title: Design and validation of a multisensory game-based tooth brushing education tool for children with visual and hearing impairment
abstract: BACKGROUND: Children with sensory disabilities exhibit a poor oral hygiene and a high prevalence of gingivitis and dental caries. Tailored multisensory oral health education interventions may improve tooth brushing skills and oral health. To develop and validate a multisensory game-based educational intervention to teach tooth brushing to children with visual and hearing impairments. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A developmental research design was used. A prototype was developed after literature review and expert interviews. This was validated by dentists and special educators and field tested among 15 children with visual impairment and 15 with hearing impairment with 7 play sessions over 4 weeks. Comprehensibility and acceptability were assessed through structured feedback, and effectiveness was measured by evaluating tooth brushing skills. title: Sawdust–plaster cast mixture versus traditional cast: Which type reduced pain and increases comfort and enhancing healing process among patients with twisting: A randomized controlled clinical trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Musculoskeletal twisting injuries, such as strains and sprains, are common and can be treated using cast immobilization without the need for surgery. The study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of Sawdust–Plaster Cast Mixture Versus Traditional Cast: Which Type Reduced Pain and Increases Comfort and Enhancing the healing process among Patients with Twisting. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The study was conducted from May to August 2025 and used a single-blind, true experimental design. Sixty patients with twisting injuries were randomly assigned to either the intervention group ( n = 29), which received the sawdust–plaster cast, or the control group ( n = 31), which received a standard cast. Pain and comfort levels were assessed using a visual analog scale (VAS), and the healing duration was recorded. Statistical analysis was performed using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) version 30. title: Comparing the pain relief effectiveness of intravenous magnesium sulfate and ketorolac versus intravenous morphine and ketorolac for kidney stones
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pain is one of the most common symptoms in various diseases. While morphine is widely used for pain relief, its adverse effects and potential for misuse have led to the exploration of safer alternatives. This study aimed to compare the analgesic effectiveness of intravenous magnesium sulfate versus morphine, both in combination with ketorolac, in patients with renal colic. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this double-blind randomized controlled trial, 174 patients with renal colic referred to the emergency department of Shahid Ganjiyan Hospital in Dezful were enrolled. Patients were randomly allocated into two equal groups ( n = 87). The intervention group received intravenous magnesium sulfate (50 mg/kg diluted in 100 mL normal saline over 15 minutes) plus ketorolac (30 mg), while the control group received intravenous morphine (0.1 mg/kg) plus ketorolac (30 mg). Pain intensity was measured using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) at baseline (admission), and 20, 40, and 60 minutes after drug administration. Demographic data were also collected. title: Impact of music therapy on diabetes distress and bio-physiological parameters in patients with diabetic foot ulcer
abstract: BACKGROUND: Diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) is a common and significant complication of uncontrolled diabetes mellitus (DM), frequently resulting in increased physiological suffering and emotional burden. Music therapy, as a complementary intervention, has shown potential in lowering stress and improving general well-being, but its influence on patients with DFU is unknown. The present study aimed to identify the impact of music therapy on diabetes distress and bio-physiological parameters among patients with DFU. METHODS AND MATERIALS: The study was conducted in a selected tertiary care hospital in South India, and a Quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group research design was used. A non-probability purposive sampling was used to select 159 participants with DFU into three groups: Group I (n = 53) received patient-selected music therapy, Group II (n = 53) received researcher-selected music, and the control group (n = 53) received routine treatment only. The intervention involved listening to music for 20 minutes twice daily over 21 consecutive days, along with standard medical care. title: Navigating the PhD thesis journey: A qualitative study of doctoral students and supervisors at a medical university in Iran
abstract: BACKGROUND: The PhD thesis serves as a cornerstone of doctoral education, yet it is often accompanied by considerable stress and inefficiencies for both students and supervisors. Although global research has extensively addressed issues such as supervision quality, institutional support, and student well-being, there is limited investigation into these dynamics from a qualitative perspective in non-Western academic settings. This study examines the lived experiences of doctoral students and their supervisors at Isfahan University of Medical Sciences to identify challenges and propose tailored reforms for this specific context. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Employing a qualitative exploratory design, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 54 participants (31 PhD students and 23 faculty supervisors) chosen through purposive sampling. The collected data underwent conventional content analysis, with themes integrated across both groups to form a unified framework. title: The impact of group cognitive behavioral therapy on stress and psychological adjustment among cigarette, e-cigarette, and hookah smokers
abstract: BACKGROUND: The tobacco epidemic remains one of the world’s major public health threats, causing preventable cancers and disabilities, and claiming over seven million lives each year. Over the past decade, the use of nicotine-containing electronic cigarettes has grown among adolescents and young adults. This study investigates the effectiveness of a group cognitive behavioral therapy program on stress and psychological adjustment among university students who want to quit smoking cigarettes or hookah. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The sample included 123 male students who smoked cigarettes and e-cigarettes and 134 students who smoked hookah, all of whom expressed a desire to quit smoking. Students who smoke both cigarettes and hookah were excluded from the study to ensure clear differentiation between the two groups of users. A nonprobability sampling method was used. Psychological stress and psychological adjustments were measured twice: before the group treatment program began and after the program was completed. title: Impact of oil fortification with iron in the prevention of anemia—A systematic review
abstract: Micronutrient malnutrition has gained its significant influence on public health and a role in the worldwide disease burden in recent years. Through fortification, the nutritional profile of staple foods is enhanced, making them more nutritious and beneficial for consumption. This systematic review aims to assess the impact of oil fortification with iron in anemia prevention. Electronic search through five databases and additional resources was performed by using the appropriate keywords. title: Determinant factors of sexual and reproductive health literacy among adolescents in Indonesia: A national population-based study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sexual and reproductive health literacy (SRHL) among adolescents is a global public health concern. Almost half of all new cases of sexually transmitted infections have been associated with health literacy among youth. Limited SRHL has led to negative behaviours and their impact on health-related outcomes. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to identify the determinants of SRHL among adolescents in Indonesia. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study drew on the most recent nationwide, population-based cross-sectional study and applied Nutbeam’s functional health literacy framework. SRHL was determined as a composite index and classified into three levels: limited, inadequate, and adequate. Pearson’s Chi-square test was used to determine the different proportions of SRHL. Binary logistic regression with a complex survey design was used to evaluate the factors associated with SRHL. title: The relationship between health literacy and the adoption of preventive behaviors against high blood pressure among villagers: A cross-sectional study in Iran
abstract: BACKGROUND: Considering the limited number of studies on health literacy among the rural population, the necessity of measuring the level of health literacy, and the increasing number of patients with hypertension, the present study aimed to determine the relationship between health literacy and the adoption of preventive behaviors in high blood pressure among the villagers. abstract: BACKGROUND: Failure to thrive (FTT) refers to inadequate growth caused by an inability to acquire or use enough calories for growth. It refers to a failure to develop over time, which can lead to more serious problems in adulthood if left untreated. FTT is a significant global health concern, particularly in developing countries like Iran. Effective FTT management necessitates timely, inclusive, and precise data on children’s FTT status. A pediatric FTT registry system is a useful tool for gathering and managing data on children with FTT. This study proposes a pediatric FTT registry system for Iran. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A developmental-applied study was conducted in three phases during 2024. title: Telenutrition health education program to increase nutritional awareness, attitude, and dietary diversity among secondary high school adolescent girls in rural area of Bangladesh: A quasi-experimental study protocol
abstract: BACKGROUND: Telenutrition, using telehealth technologies for remote nutritional care, has proven effective in primary care. Nutritional deficiencies constitute a global health burden, characterized by chronic undernutrition and micronutrient deficiencies, especially in adolescent girls in impoverished nations such as Bangladesh. Telenutrition, which uses digital technologies to provide remote nutritional treatment, is a promising strategy to decrease this burden. This study aims to determine the impact of telenutrition education on improving nutritional awareness, attitude, and dietary diversity among school going adolescent girls in rural Bangladesh. title: Artificial intelligence and its impact on oral health care education. A randomized study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI)-generated educational materials demonstrate superior effectiveness in improving patient comprehension and reducing anxiety compared to traditional methods. title: Health behavior and hygiene practices among islamic boarding school students in Indonesia: A qualitative study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Islamic boarding schools in Indonesia are essential for religious and character education, yet health behavior and hygiene practices (HBHP) among students remain limited, leading to preventable illnesses. This study aimed to explore HBHP in boarding schools, identify supporting and inhibiting factors, and examine the role of community health centers (CHCs) in promoting student health. title: Investigating the effect of vitamin C supplementation on bacterial vaginosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Bacterial vaginosis (BV), the most common type of vaginitis, results from reduced vaginal lactobacilli and increased anaerobic bacteria. Vitamin C may aid BV treatment by promoting lactic acid production. This study evaluated the effectiveness of vitamin C in treating BV. To this aim, a systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Iranian databases identified randomized clinical trials published up to October 29, 2024. The protocol for this systematic review is registered. Risk of bias was assessed using the Verhagen tool. Mean differences and their 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using the random-effects model. title: Localizing the main components of competencies in high-level managers based on health system evaluation indicators: Content analysis approach
abstract: BACKGROUND: Managers play a key role in organizations. Competence of managers has become an important issue for organizations. This issue is very important for high-level managers in health-oriented organizations. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to identify and determine the components and analyze the core competencies of high-level managers in the field of health in medical sciences universities of the country, with the approach of content analysis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This qualitative study was conducted using the content analysis method in 2023-2024. Data collection included retrieving documents from relevant databases. title: The effect of self-study training on resilience and effective coping style of women involved in domestic violence
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a serious yet preventable public health issue. Resilience plays a significant role in helping women overcome the effects of IPV. abstract: BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of preventable deaths among Nigerian women, largely due to poor awareness and low Pap smear uptake. Empowering nurses to deliver focused educational interventions may bridge this gap. This study assessed the effectiveness of a nurse-led educational intervention in improving knowledge of cervical cancer and promoting Pap smear screening among women in Cross River State, Nigeria. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A single-blind, parallel-group randomized controlled trial using a pre-test/post-test non-equivalent control design was conducted among 306 women selected through multistage sampling. Participants were assigned to intervention ( n = 153) and control ( n = 153) groups. abstract: BACKGROUND: Exclusive breastfeeding is a cornerstone of neonatal survival, yet rates in Iraq remain below international targets. title: Student-supervisor relationship and suicidal behavior among Chinese medical postgraduates: The mediating effect of insomnia and depression
abstract: BACKGROUND: Suicidal behavior is a leading mental health concern among medical students, particularly in China where postgraduates face intense academic pressure and hierarchical dependence on supervisors. title: Trends, collaboration, and impact of scientific research on the Mediterranean diet during pregnancy
abstract: BACKGROUND: The Mediterranean diet (MED) is well recognized for its general health benefits and, specifically, during pregnancy, where it may reduce risks such as gestational diabetes, intrauterine growth restriction, preterm birth, and low birth weight. It is also associated with improved maternal metabolic, psychological, and immune outcomes. This study analyzes the scientific production on MED during pregnancy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: descriptive bibliometric study was conducted on original articles addressing MED in pregnant women, published in Scopus (2015-2024). abstract: BACKGROUND: The rapid growth of the elderly population in Iran has made studying the mental and behavioral health challenges of the elderly and their home caregivers a necessity for health policymaking; in this regard, the study was conducted with the aim of identifying the behavioral and mental health problems and resilience of home caregivers and the elderly. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The research was conducted with a qualitative content analysis approach and with a purposeful sampling of 15 elderly people in need of care and 18 home caregivers. abstract: Adolescent pregnancy remains a global public health issue associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, educational disruption, and long-term socioeconomic consequences. abstract: BACKGROUND: Given the anesthesia team’s crucial role and the necessity of strong pre-anesthesia knowledge for nurse anesthesia students’ patient safety, innovative teaching methods are vital for enhancing their ability to maintain safety and improve care. Effective Information, Education, and Communication (IEC) materials tailored for young people are limited, particularly in culturally diverse low- and middle-income settings. title: Psychometric properties of the Persian version of the National Stressful Events Survey PTSD Short Scale based on DSM-5 in betrayed women
abstract: BACKGROUND: Betrayal trauma, such as marital infidelity, often leads to significant psychological distress, including symptoms consistent with posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Reliable and culturally relevant tools are essential for assessing PTSD in affected populations. This study aimed to evaluate the psychometric properties and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) of the Persian version of the National Stressful Events Survey PTSD Short Scale (NSESSS-PTSD) in women experiencing marital betrayal. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study assessed the Persian NSESSS-PTSD among 128 women attending psychological clinics in Tehran, Iran. Participants were selected using convenience sampling. The mean age of participants was 35.4 years (SD = 7.8). Research tools included the 9-item NSESSS-PTSD, PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5), Impact of Event Scale-Revised (IES-R), Psychological Well-Being Scale (PWB), and Subjective Happiness Scale (SHS). Data were analyzed using SPSS and AMOS (version 26). Reliability was evaluated through Cronbach’s alpha (internal consistency) and test–retest methods. title: Modelling the risk of conversion from mild cognitive impairment to Alzheimer’s disease using machine learning
abstract: BACKGROUND: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is a transitional state between normal aging and dementia, characterized by subtle cognitive decline. While not all individuals with MCI will progress to Alzheimer’s disease (AD), early identification of those at high risk is crucial for timely interventions. Machine learning algorithms offer a promising approach for analyzing complex datasets, including neuroimaging and cognitive assessments, to predict the likelihood of progression to AD. In this study, we evaluate 12 Machine Learning algorithms to predict the risk of progression from MCI to AD and identify the most important features contributing to this progression. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We selected 899 MCI subjects (596 stable, 303 progressive) from the AD Neuroimaging Initiative dataset. ML algorithms were used to predict the progression based on predictive features, including cognitive measures, demographic variables, and neuroimaging biomarkers. title: The effect of psychoeducational intervention on nomophobia among university students in the north-eastern region of India: A quasi-experimental study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Nomophobia, the irrational fear of being without a mobile phone or internet connection, is increasingly common among undergraduate students, contributing to psychological distress and impaired academic performance. This study evaluated the effectiveness of a psychoeducational intervention in reducing nomophobia levels in this population. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test design was employed with 217 undergraduate students. Nomophobia levels were assessed using a validated scale. The intervention, delivered in multiple sessions, focused on raising awareness about mobile dependency, its psychological effects, and coping strategies. title: Consumer-driven cosmetovigilance: A cross-sectional survey on risk perceptions and public health implications in the United Arab Emirates
abstract: BACKGROUND: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) represents one of the fastest-growing cosmetics markets in the Middle East, yet little is known about consumer awareness of cosmetic safety and cosmetovigilance practices. This study aims to evaluate cosmetic use, safety awareness, adverse effects, and perceptions of cosmetovigilance among the general population in the northern emirates of the UAE. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was conducted from December 2023 to March 2024 among 615 residents of Ras Al Khaimah, UAE. Data were collected using a validated bilingual questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive statistics, Chi-square tests, and logistic regression to examine associations between sociodemographic factors and cosmetic knowledge. RESULTS: Of 615 participants, 62.6% were female, and the median age was 35 years. The most frequently used products were creams (52.8%) and deodorants/perfumes (48.7%). Reported adverse effects included itching (32.0%, n = 197), headaches (19.2%, n = 118), rashes (11.5%, n = 71), and hair loss (11.5%, n = 71). title: Risk factors for diabetic peripheral neuropathy in diabetes mellitus patients: A case-control study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic illness that can lead to complications such as Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy (DPN). Identifying risk factors for DPN is crucial for prevention and management. The study aims to enhance understanding of the underlying mechanisms contributing to DPN and to inform targeted interventions that can improve patient outcomes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study utilized a quantitative, case-control design involving 108 patients with diabetes mellitus at the Regional Hospital Dr. Moewardi. Members were alienated hooked on two groups: those with diabetic motor neuropathy and those without. Data were collected through direct physical examinations and questionnaires assessing smoking history, duration of diabetes, education level, and self-management compliance. Statistical analyses, including Chi-square tests and logistic reversion, were performed to evaluate the relationships between these factors and the incidence of DPN. title: Optimizing the drug supply chain in hospitals: A mixed-method study in Iran
abstract: BACKGROUND: The management of the drug supply chain (DSC) is crucial for the success of the healthcare system in ensuring the health of the population. This study aimed to examine the factors affecting the DSC in hospitals across Iran. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This mixed-methods study was conducted in 2024 at a large teaching hospital in Tehran. The study population included hospital administrators and healthcare professionals. The most important criterion for inclusion in the study was having sufficient knowledge and experience. Data were collected using a researcher-developed questionnaire of 28 items across five dimensions. Data analysis was performed using SPSS and AMOS software. title: Efficacy of new a novel sawdust-plaster material related to improved pain reduction and healing among fracture patients: A randomized clinical trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute fractures often require prolonged immobilization, which is frequently associated with significant pain and physical discomfort. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of an innovative birch sawdust–plaster mixture in reducing pain and improving clinical outcomes compared with traditional plaster of Paris. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A single-blind, true experimental design was conducted between May and September 2025 in Baghdad, Iraq. A total of 56 adult patients with upper limb fractures who met the inclusion criteria were recruited and randomly allocated into two groups: the intervention group ( n = 27, sawdust-plaster back-slab) and the control group ( n = 29, traditional back-slab). Randomization was achieved using sequentially numbered, opaque, sealed envelopes. Data were collected using a sociodemographic sheet and the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS). Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS version 30 employing independent t-tests and Chi-square tests to compare outcomes. title: Actions speak louder than words: Correlation between cancer patients’ perceptions of rights implementation and nursing care satisfaction

title: “Are nurses ready for dementia care? Insights into knowledge, attitudes, and practice”
abstract: BACKGROUND: Dementia is a severe global health issue closely related to population aging. title: Team-based learning and its impact on clinical reasoning in medical education: A review and the unexplored role of artificial intelligence
abstract: Team-based learning (TBL) is widely adopted in medical education to promote active learning, collaboration, and improved clinical reasoning. Although digital platforms are increasingly integrated into TBL, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in this context remains largely theoretical. We systematically reviewed empirical studies evaluating the effectiveness of TBL on clinical reasoning skills among medical students. Searches were conducted using PubMed with Boolean operators targeting terms such as “team-based learning,” “clinical reasoning,” “AI,” and “medical education.” After screening 21 studies, 16 met the inclusion criteria. Data were extracted on study design, participants, TBL interventions, assessment methods, and presence of digital or AI tools. Of the 16 studies included, none employed true AI-based interventions. title: Pharmacological therapy and dietary intervention for obesity management: A one-year prospective cohort study in Baghdad
abstract: BACKGROUND: Evidence directly comparing long-term pharmacological therapy and structured dietary intervention for obesity in Middle Eastern populations is limited. This study provides 12-month real-world comparative data from specialized obesity clinics in Baghdad, Iraq. title: Fatigue, anthropometric profile, and health-related quality of life among fifth-year medical students: A single-center cross-sectional study from Kazakhstan
abstract: BACKGROUND: Fatigue is a familiar problem in medical training, and a growing body of work has linked it to worse academic performance and lower psycho-emotional well-being. Few data are available for Central Asian student cohorts. We set out to measure the prevalence of fatigue in a single fifth-year cohort and to test how it relates to body mass index (BMI), physical activity, and self-reported quality of life (QoL). MATERIALS AND METHODS: Cross-sectional, single-center survey conducted in the middle of the academic semester at a medical faculty in Kazakhstan, on fifth-year students only. Two hundred and sixty-nine fifth-year medical students completed the survey. title: The influence of emotional intelligence and resilience on academic burnout of rehabilitation students with mediating effect of stress: A study demands-resources model perspective
abstract: BACKGROUND: Academic burnout, conceptualized as an extension of career burnout, manifests in students during the learning process through symptoms such as emotional exhaustion, depersonalization tendencies, and a sense of low personal accomplishment. This study aimed to explore the impact of emotional intelligence (EI), resilience, and stress on academic burnout grounded in the Study Demands-Resources (SD-R) model. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional design incorporating structural equation modeling was employed. The sample consisted of 760 rehabilitation students from three medical science universities in Iran, with 27% male and 73% female participants. RESULTS: Findings revealed that EI and resilience—both considered academic resources—had significant negative direct effects on academic burnout. In contrast, stress, as an academic demand, demonstrated a significant positive direct effect. Furthermore, both resources exhibited significant indirect effects on academic burnout through the mediating role of stress. title: Anthropometric profile, hypertension, and lifestyle risk factors: A cross-sectional study among Kurdish medical students
abstract: BACKGROUND: Medical students, as future healthcare professionals, should model healthy lifestyle behaviors. However, their own practices and health profiles often fall short of optimal standards. This study assessed anthropometric measures, lifestyle habits, and clinical risk factors for non-communicable diseases among Kurdish medical students. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 280 undergraduate medical students (80 males, 200 females) aged 18–24 years at Hawler Medical University. Data were collected using a two-part approach: (1) direct clinical assessments for anthropometrics (height, weight), blood pressure (BP), and random blood glucose (RBG); and (2) a pre-validated, structured questionnaire to document diet, physical activity, smoking, and sleep patterns. title: Cardiac camp: An outreach program to build health literacy among underrepresented in medicine adolescents and increase diversity in medicine
abstract: BACKGROUND: Eliminating racial and ethnic disparities in cardiovascular disease (CVD) requires multilevel action, including improving health literacy and diversifying the healthcare workforce. To contribute to this goal, UCSF medical students designed an immersive summer camp to teach underrepresented minority backgrounds in medical professions (URM) high school students about CVD and encourage interest in healthcare careers. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A stipend-supported, 1-week cardiology summer camp for URM Bay Area high school students was implemented by medical students. journal_name: Journal of Education and Health Promotion
title: Managing public education on smoking behavior in families with stunted children: Between challenges and opportunities in Indonesia
abstract: BACKGROUND: Stunting remains a major public health concern in Indonesia, compounded by the country’s high prevalence of smoking. This study explores the smoking behavior of families with stunted children, parental knowledge of smoking-related risks, and their motivation for behavioral change. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using a qualitative approach, data were collected through interviews, observations, documentation, and focus group discussions in East Nusa Tenggara and Aceh—two provinces with high stunting rates. RESULTS: Findings reveal that most fathers are active smokers and frequently smoke around pregnant women or children. Parental awareness of the link between cigarette smoke and stunting is limited, and fathers show low motivation to quit smoking even after stunting is diagnosed. CONCLUSIONS: The study recommends revising national stunting reduction strategies to include smoking prevention, enforcing smoke-free policies, restricting cigarette advertising and sales, and empowering families—especially fathers—to change harmful smoking behaviors to protect child health.

title: The effect of virtual and in-person education on pain management and quality of life of university students with dysmenorrhea
abstract: BACKGROUND: Dysmenorrhea affects daily life, mental health, and productivity, raising economic and social concerns. It also significantly affects women’s productivity and quality of life. This study aimed to compare the effectiveness of virtual and in-person education in reducing pain and improving quality of life among university students with primary dysmenorrhea. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This quasiexperimental study involved 112 university students with moderate to severe dysmenorrhea (a pain score of 4 or higher over two consecutive menstrual cycles), who were randomly assigned to either In-Person or virtual education groups. An educational intervention was conducted in a 1-hour session (covering topics such as menstrual physiology, nutritional modifications, nonpharmacological treatments, and suitable exercises to alleviate menstrual pain) before their first menstrual cycle. Data were collected using the SF-36 questionnaire, Visual Analog Scale (VAS), and McGill Pain Questionnaire and analyzed with SPSS software. title: Study protocol for effects of prone spinal decompression therapy in addition to Mckenzie exercises versus Mckenzie exercises only on pain and functional disability in lumbar radiculopathy–A randomized clinical trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Lumbar radiculopathy, which affects both men and women equally, are associated with symptoms of back and leg pain that significantly impairs body functioning, walking ability, and quality of life. Therefore, determining the optimal treatment protocol is necessary. The objective of the study is to evaluate the efficacy of prone spinal decompression therapy (SDT) combined with McKenzie exercises compared with McKenzie exercises alone on pain and functional disability in patients diagnosed with lumbar radiculopathy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A single-blinded randomized clinical trial will be conducted using simple randomization at university physiotherapy department. According to sample size calculation, we aim to recruit 44 participants aged between 25 and 55 years with lumbar radiculopathy. Participants will be allocated using computer generated method and will be randomized into 2 groups: Group A (SDT + McKenzie) and Group B (McKenzie only) and each session will be lasted for 20–30 min. title: Comparing the efficacy of LORETA neurofeedback versus cognitive rehabilitation on working memory in children with learning disorders: A double-blind clinical trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Nowadays, researchers emphasize the use of inexpensive and low-risk methods as preferred treatments for disorders in children and adolescents. The present study was conducted with the aim of comparing the effects of LORETA neurofeedback (NF) and cognitive rehabilitation on the working memory of children with learning disabilities. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The present research design was a quasi-experimental with pretest, posttest with three-month follow-up. The population were all students with learning disorders and sample was 45 children aged between 7 and 10 with learning disabilities from schools in Shiraz. Three groups of 15 children were selected by convenience sampling. The intervention consisted of cognitive rehabilitation and LORETA NF training sessions. title: Misoprostol monotherapy versus adjunctive mechanical cervical ripening with Foley catheter or Dilapan-S for second-trimester termination of pregnancy: A randomized controlled trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: In regions where mifepristone access is legally or logistically constrained, second-trimester pregnancy termination predominantly relies on misoprostol-only regimens. However, these protocols are often associated with a prolonged induction-to-abortion interval (IAI). This study evaluated whether integrating mechanical cervical ripening agents—specifically Foley catheters or Dilapan-S rods—could enhance the clinical efficiency of misoprostol-induced terminations in mifepristone-restricted settings. title: Identifying the requirements for the implementation of teledentistry in rural areas: A scoping review protocol
abstract: Oral health disparities in rural areas of developing countries are exacerbated by geographic barriers, limited infrastructure, and workforce shortages. Teledentistry, a branch of telemedicine, offers a promising solution to improve access to dental care. This scoping review aims to identify the infrastructure, workforce, and patient-related requirements for implementing teledentistry in rural settings. In this scoping review, Arksey and O’Malley’s five-stage framework will be used. PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Embase databases will be used to search for studies using a detailed search strategy. Using specified inclusion and exclusion criteria, studies that focus on identifying the challenges of implementing teledentistry in rural areas, and were published between 2004 and 2024, will be identified and reviewed. An interdisciplinary team will develop search strategies, and two researchers will independently review eligible studies for final study selection.
